findings.title: Plaintext passwords and PII are written to logs on signup
findings.explanation: The PR description says the logger already redacts sensitive fields. That is not true. `src/lib/logger.ts` redacts only `authorization` and `token`, so `password` is not redacted. Every signup attempt would write the user's plaintext password to stdout, along with their email and organization name. These logs usually go to aggregators with broad access and long retention. This is a credential leak. It also breaks the rule in `docs/CONVENTIONS.md` (line 23): never log request bodies or headers on auth routes. Remove this line. To debug validation failures, log only the failure details, for example the zod issue paths and codes from `safeParse`, the list of keys received, and the types or lengths of the values. Never log the values themselves.

findings.title: Validation failures are not handled, so failed signups stay opaque
findings.explanation: `signupSchema.parse` throws on invalid input. The PR's goal is to see why signups fail, but the real information is in the ZodError. Use `safeParse` and log `error.issues`, keeping only `path` and `code`, since messages can echo input. Return a 400 with the field errors. Logging the issues also fixes the debugging problem without recording secrets. Check that an Express error handler exists, because an async handler that throws may otherwise produce an unhandled rejection (depending on the Express version) or a 500.

findings.title: Redaction list is an unsafe base for logging request data
findings.explanation: A denylist of two keys is fragile. `password`, `secret`, `api_key` and `password_confirmation` all pass through unredacted. If body logging is ever added anywhere, switch to an allowlist or extend the denylist (`password`, `passwd`, `secret`, `cookie`, `api_key`, and similar). Also fix the misleading claim in the PR description.
